findings.title: Symlink is followed and its target hashed
quotes: a symlink is never listed or followed
findings.fix: skip any entry where `is_symlink()` is true before `is_file()`, and test it.

sources.situation: a tracked or untracked `README.md` that is a symlink to a file outside the repo, such as `~/.ssh/id_rsa`. `scan` checks `(Path(root) / f).is_file()`, which follows symlinks, then calls `read_bytes()` on the target. It lists the symlink under `product-docs` with a hash of the outside file. That reads data from outside the repo, and the hash lets someone confirm a guess at that file's contents. A symlink to a directory or a missing target is dropped silently.

A tracked symlink named `README.md` that points outside the repo passes `(Path(root) / f).is_file()`, because `is_file()` follows links. It is listed, and `read_bytes()` hashes the target, which can be outside the repo. CT-1 and FR-3 say a symlink is never listed or followed.

findings.title: Outside a git repo the scan reports success with "nothing found"
quotes: not inside a git work tree → exit 1, `nio onboard scan needs a git repository`
findings.fix: call `records.git(..., full=True)`, and on a non-zero code exit 1 with the contract message.

sources.situation: `nio onboard scan` runs in a plain directory. `records.git` calls `subprocess.run` without checking the return code and returns the stdout lines, which are empty on failure. `scan` prints `no candidate files found` and exits 0. The dev, or the onboard skill, concludes the project has no docs or manifests when the scan never ran. The skill may then treat the project as empty and start the `--empty` path, with no error shown.

`records.git` returns `r.stdout.splitlines()` and ignores the exit code, so a failed `git ls-files` gives an empty list. `scan` then prints `no candidate files found` and exits 0. The dev gets a false "empty project" answer, and no test covers the failure.

`records.git` returns `r.stdout.splitlines()`, which is `[]` when git fails. In a non-git directory the scan therefore prints "no candidate files found" and exits 0. This hides a real failure and is indistinguishable from AC-4's empty repo. No test covers it.

findings.reason: `records.git` returns `r.stdout.splitlines()` and ignores the exit code unless `full=True`. `onboard.scan` calls it without `full`, so a non-git directory prints "no candidate files found" and exits 0, not the CT-2 exit 1. No task in the plan defers this.

findings.title: Non-ASCII or quoted paths are dropped silently
quotes: Candidates are `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard` (tracked and untracked, not ignored)
findings.fix: use `ls-files -z` and split on NUL. The output line also needs unambiguous handling of paths with spaces, since the output is `<category> <path> <hash>`.

sources.situation: the call omits `-z` and does not turn off `core.quotePath`. A path such as `docs/résumé.md`, or any path with a tab, comes back from git as a quoted, escaped string (`"docs/r\303\251sum\303\251.md"`). The `is_file()` check fails on that string, so the file is left out with no warning. The final count is still "N candidate files", so the dev sees a plausible but incomplete list. A newline in a name would split one path into two lines the same way.

findings.reason: `scan` runs `ls-files -co --exclude-standard` without `-z` and without `core.quotepath=off`. Git then returns quoted, escaped paths for non-ASCII names, `(Path(root)/f).is_file()` fails on them, and the files are dropped silently.

findings.title: No secrets handling, and the category lists are well short of the contract
quotes: `SECRETS` is the list FR-24 quotes, matched against the base name.
findings.fix: build the contract's `CATEGORIES` and `SECRETS` with `fnmatch`, and add the `--others --ignored` pass for secrets only.

sources.situation: there is no `SECRETS` list and no `secrets` category. A secrets-named file that also matches a category, or a git-ignored `.env`, gets no path-only entry. A matching file is hashed and listed under the other category: the contract says it must show only as `("secrets", path, "")`, and it would instead carry a content hash. `CATS` lacks `.cursor/rules/*.mdc`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.windsurfrules`, `.clinerules`, `.kiro/steering/*`, `Pulumi.yaml`, `cdk.json`, `Chart.yaml`, `fly.toml`, `Jenkinsfile`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `.circleci/config.yml`, `build.gradle*`, `requirements*.txt` and `docs/adr/*`. It also treats every file under `.github/workflows/` as CI, and every `docs/**/*.md` as implementation-docs where CT-1 says product-docs. Files like these are skipped with no output, and a hash of a secret file leaks.

findings.title: Output order and the CLI shape don't match the contract, and the contract tests are missing
findings.fix: return the sorted tuples from `scan` and print them in the CLI layer. Land the remaining CT items, or mark them out of this epic's scope.

sources.situation: `scan` sorts by path only and prints directly. It does not return the `list[tuple]` that CT-1 and the later `stale` and `to_reconcile` functions need. Consumers such as CT-11 `to_reconcile` cannot reuse it, so each would reparse stdout. `test_scan_skips_symlink`, `test_scan_secrets_path_only` and `test_scan_more_secret_names` are listed in the results but absent from tests/test_onboard.py. The journey `nio pack ... --reader worker` fails with `unrecognized arguments: --reader worker`, so the reader packs, status lines, `start`/`confirm`/`pause`/`skip`, `backup` and `changed` are not in the diff at all.

with `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `README.md`, the output is `implementation-docs ARCHITECTURE.md`, then `agent-docs CLAUDE.md`, then `product-docs README.md`, which is path order, not category then path. The `scan` function also prints and returns `None`, so a later caller that expects the list in CT-1 (CT-3, CT-7, CT-11) gets nothing to iterate. The table is called `CATS` in the diff and `CATEGORIES` in CT-1.

`scan` only prints and returns nothing. CT-1 wants it to return a sorted `list[tuple]` that CT-3, CT-9 and CT-11 can reuse. The `SECRETS` list and the git-ignored-file pass are also absent. If the CT-4 and CT-11 tasks need this return value, they will have to rework `scan`.

`CATS` has no secrets category and `scan` has no `SECRETS` list. `scan` only lists files in the existing categories and only through `git ls-files --exclude-standard`. Files FR-24 lists, such as `.env`, are therefore never reported as path-only entries, and git-ignored ones are never seen. Any secret-named file whose name also matches a category would be hashed with its content-derived hash instead of `("secrets", path, "")`. The dev never learns that onboarding found a secrets file and kept it out. CT-11's `seen` and `to_reconcile` logic also depends on this category existing.

findings.reason: implementation-E-1-consistency: the sort and CLI-shape parts are fixed, but the remaining CT items are not all landed: CT-1's symlink and non-regular-file exclusion has no test in `tests/test_onboard.py`, and CT-2's `secrets <path>` line is not asserted through the CLI (the secrets test checks the Python tuple repr only).
findings.note: the two tests are planned in T-13 (TC-13, TC-19, TC-48), epic E-4; the code already does it

sources.situation: a repo whose only candidates are `.clinerules` and `Jenkinsfile` makes `scan` print `no candidate files found`, which is false. The same happens for `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `Pulumi.yaml` and `build.gradle`. `README.rst` is not listed, and `requirements-dev.txt` is not listed because only the exact name `requirements.txt` matches.

findings.title: The exit-code assertion in the ignored-files test is never enforced
quotes: assert code == 0 and "candidate files" in out or "no candidate" in out, out
findings.fix: write `assert code == 0 and ("candidate files" in out or "no candidate" in out), out`.

sources.situation: `and` binds tighter than `or`, so the test passes whenever the output contains "no candidate", whatever the exit code. A scan that exits 1 with that text in its output passes the check.

findings.title: Category matching is narrower than CT-1 and misroutes `docs/*.md`
findings.fix: implement `CATEGORIES` as `fnmatch` patterns matched against the path and the base name, as CT-1 specifies.

findings.title: The skip test's assertion passes whatever the scan prints
quotes: assert code == 0 and "candidate files" in out or "no candidate" in out, out
findings.fix: parenthesise the condition, assert `code == 0`, and add a legitimate `README.md` that must still be listed.

sources.situation: `and` binds tighter than `or`, so this reads `(code == 0 and A) or B`. It passes on a non-zero exit as long as the output contains "no candidate". The path assertion on the next line is what actually checks AC-3. The test also never creates a listable file next to the ignored ones, so it cannot show that the scan still lists real files while skipping the ignored ones.

findings.title: Output is sorted by path only and git's quoting is not undone
findings.fix: use `ls-files -z`, or `-c core.quotepath=off`, and sort the entries by `(category, path)`.

sources.situation: `sorted(set(...))` orders by path only. For the quoting, git without `-z` and with the default `core.quotepath` returns paths containing non-ASCII or special characters wrapped in quotes and escaped. `Path(root)/f` then does not exist, so those files are silently dropped.

findings.title: Symlinks are followed and hashed
quotes: anything that is not a regular file inside the repo (a symlink is never listed or followed)
findings.fix: skip any path where `(Path(root)/f).is_symlink()` is true, or whose resolved path is not inside the repo root. Add a symlink test (CT-1 expects `test_scan_skips_symlink`, which is not in this diff).

sources.situation: a repo has a tracked or untracked symlink named `README.md` (or `Dockerfile`, `CLAUDE.md`) that points to a file outside the repo, such as `~/.ssh/id_rsa`. `Path.is_file()` follows the link and returns true. `scan` then runs `read_bytes()` on the target and prints `product-docs README.md <hash>`. The scan lists the link and reads a file outside the repo. A hash of a low-entropy outside file is a guessing oracle for its content.

findings.reason: Symlink skipping belongs to T-13 (AC-48), which depends on T-1, and T-1 serves only AC-1..4, so T-1 following symlinks is sequenced and not a defect of T-1.
